I really want https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/docs/+/82776/5/style/cpp/.clang-tidy to go and then we can add this on top. I don't know what the hold up on 82776 is but this looks fine.

I think this makes the code the slightest bit better, matching the docs clang-tidy is more important to me. 
If the docs clang-tidy does not want this change, I am good with your plan to make these changes but not enforce in .clang-tidy

> I think this makes the code the slightest bit better, matching the docs clang-tidy is more important to me. 

Why's that?  Considering I wrote the in-review .clang-tidy, my plan was to follow the same path with this, make sure it's useful, then enable it in the reference.

> If the docs clang-tidy does not want this change, I am good with your plan to make these changes but not enforce in .clang-tidy

>> I think this makes the code the slightest bit better, matching the docs clang-tidy is more important to me. 

> Why's that? 

bmcweb matching the overall project is more important than I think the benefit this gives us. If we need to deviate from the project, let's make sure we have a reason. (I am talking about the general case as well as this specific clang-tidy case). That said, I think we are on the same page here..

Why is it not just std::ranges::sort(paths) ? Why the reverse_view ?
Because the prior code was rbegin/rend, which reversed the sort order.  FWIW, tidy made this change automatically.
Ack. I overlooked the rbegin/rend.
These are certainly more concise..
Acknowledged
